title: The IFCASL Corpus of French and German Non-native and Native Read Speech
why_promising: Primary French-German bilingual learner and native read-speech corpus with about 100 speakers. Published corpus documentation states that phone and word boundaries were initially forced-aligned, then more than half of the data were manually re-labelled: the non-native French/German subcorpora to 80%, native French to 60%, and native German to 25%. The manually corrected Real tier contains actual phone labels and boundaries; Word boundaries were manually corrected when needed, and trained native-language annotators marked insertions, deletions, substitutions, and incorrect (de)voicing. Strong candidate for L1/L2 production, realized-vs-canonical phones, segment timing, pronunciation errors, voicing, lexical and task metadata.
open_question: Manual-annotation eligibility is well established, but this run did not locate a public downloadable deposit containing the underlying WAV/TextGrid files. Keep in HIGH review until an authoritative public repository or access route is located and file-level licensing/redistribution terms are verified. Admit only records with the Real/manual correction layer; automatic-only Align material must remain excluded.
